title: Partial derivatives preserve the polynomial evaluation kernel of a p-independent family
statement: Let $p$ be prime and $K/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] with both fields of characteristic $p$. Set $B=kK^p\subseteq K$, the subfield generated by $k$ and the $p$-th powers in $K$. Let $I$ be any index set and $t:I\to K$. Suppose the family $t^E=\prod_j t_j^{E_j}$ indexed by finitely supported $E:I\to\mathbf N$ with $E_j<p$ for every $j$ is $B$-linearly independent. For the evaluation homomorphism $e:B[X_j:j\in I]\to K$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], every $i\in I$ and polynomial $f$ satisfy $e(f)=0\Longrightarrow e(\partial f/\partial X_i)=0$, where the formal partial derivative is [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]. No spanning assumption is required.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), proof of (a) implies (b): the presentation by X_i^p - x_i^p; expanded by finite-support reduction and descent of formal partial derivatives. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07P2 on 2026-10-13.

proof.text: For each j take c_j=t_j^p in B and g_j=X_j^p-C(c_j). Let J be the ideal generated by the g_j. Evaluation kills the generators, so J is contained in its kernel. Form Q=B[X]/J and write z_j for the class of X_j, so z_j^p=c_j.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), proof of (a) implies (b): the presentation by X_i^p - x_i^p; expanded by finite-support reduction and descent of formal partial derivatives. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07P2 on 2026-10-13.

proof.text: The bounded monomials v_E=product_j z_j^{E_j} span Q over B. For any monomial r X^F, write F_j=p(F_j div p)+(F_j mod p). Its image is (r product_j c_j^{F_j div p}) times v_(F mod p). The remainder has finite support and each exponent is less than p. Polynomial induction and surjectivity of the quotient map now give the span equality.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), proof of (a) implies (b): the presentation by X_i^p - x_i^p; expanded by finite-support reduction and descent of formal partial derivatives. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07P2 on 2026-10-13.

proof.text: Evaluation induces a B-algebra homomorphism pi:Q -> K. It sends v_E to t^E. For any x in the kernel, express x as a finite linear combination of the spanning v_E. Applying pi gives a relation among t^E. Independence forces all coefficients to vanish, and hence x=0. Therefore pi is injective and ker(e)=J.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), proof of (a) implies (b): the presentation by X_i^p - x_i^p; expanded by finite-support reduction and descent of formal partial derivatives. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07P2 on 2026-10-13.

proof.text: Each partial derivative of g_j vanishes: the derivative of the constant is zero and the derivative of X_j^p has scalar factor p=0. Span induction on J, using additivity and Leibniz on arbitrary polynomial multiples of the g_j, proves partial derivatives preserve J. If e(f)=0 then f is in J, so its partial derivative evaluates to zero.

mathlib_searches.query: The kernel of evaluation on a p-independent family of field elements is stable under formal partial differentiation in characteristic p
If p-bounded monomials in t are linearly independent over a field containing all pth powers, the kernel of polynomial evaluation at t is stable under partial derivatives

theorem aeval_pderiv_eq_zero_of_pIndependent
    {k : Type u} {K : Type v} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] [CharP K p]
    {I : Type w} (t : I → K)
    (hli : LinearIndependent
      (IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range (fun x : K => x ^ p)))
      (fun E : {E : I →₀ ℕ // ∀ i : I, E i < p} =>
        E.val.prod (fun i e => t i ^ e)))
    (i : I) (f : MvPolynomial I
      (IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range (fun x : K => x ^ p))))
    (hf : aeval t f = 0) : aeval t (pderiv i f) = 0
